items.title: USPS: lost or damaged package (insured)
items.summary: Either the sender or the recipient can file a domestic claim for insured mail that is lost, damaged, or missing contents. USPS pays up to the insured amount and never more than the item's actual value. Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail and USPS Ground Advantage include up to $100 of insurance in the price.

fields.label: Who can file
fields.value: The sender or the recipient. You need the tracking or label number, proof of insurance (the mailing receipt, the outer packaging with an insured label, or the online label record) and proof of value (sales receipt, paid invoice, card statement or online order record).

fields.label: Deadline
fields.value: Damaged or missing contents: file right away, and no later than 60 days after the mailing date. Lost item: Priority Mail Express from 7 days after mailing; Priority Mail, USPS Ground Advantage, insured mail, COD and Registered Mail from 15 days after mailing; all no later than 60 days after the mailing date.

fields.label: What you get
fields.value: Payment of the item's value up to the insured amount, in full or in part. USPS does not pay more than the actual value. Decisions usually arrive within 5 to 10 days; approved claims are paid within 7 to 10 business days. Uninsured items are not paid; use a Missing Mail search for those.

fields.label: Included insurance
fields.value: Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail and USPS Ground Advantage include up to $100 of insurance when the shipment has a USPS tracking barcode. Coverage up to $5,000 can be bought at a Post Office or online.

fields.label: How to claim
fields.value: File online with a free USPS.com account; you can save a draft and get status emails. For a paper claim form call 1-800-332-0317 (Mon-Fri, 6 AM-6 PM CT). Keep the damaged item and all packaging; USPS may ask you to bring the whole package to a Post Office for inspection. If the claim is denied, appeal within 30 days of the decision, and a final appeal within 30 days after that.

items.title: USPS: Priority Mail Express delivered late
items.summary: Priority Mail Express comes with a money-back guarantee. If the item missed the guaranteed delivery date or time printed on the receipt, you can request a refund of the Priority Mail Express postage.

fields.label: Who can file
fields.value: The USPS refund page does not say who may request a Priority Mail Express refund. You need the tracking number and the mailing receipt.

fields.label: Deadline
fields.value: 2 to 30 days after the mailing date for Priority Mail Express without extra services. 30 to 60 days after the mailing date if an extra service was bought with it.

fields.label: What you get
fields.value: A refund of the Priority Mail Express postage for mail that did not arrive by the guaranteed time. Only one refund request per tracking number; any extra-service refund must be combined into the same request. Approved online refunds are mailed as a check; Post Office refunds can be paid in cash, check or money order. Exceptions apply (DMM 604.9.5).

fields.label: How to claim
fields.value: Request online with a free USPS.com account, or fill out Part I of PS Form 3533 in duplicate at any Post Office and hand it in with your customer copy of Label 11. A partly paid or denied request can be disputed within 30 days of the decision.

items.title: USPS: package missing (Missing Mail search)
items.summary: If a USPS item has not arrived, you can ask USPS to search for it. Search requests can be submitted starting 7 days after the mailing date. USPS does not pay for uninsured lost or damaged items, so a search is the way to try to recover them.

fields.label: Who can file
fields.value: Anyone with the item details. You will need the sender and recipient mailing addresses, the size and type of the package or envelope, the tracking number or mailing date, a description of the contents (brand, model, color, size) and pictures that could help identify the item.

fields.label: Deadline
fields.value: Start a search from 7 days after the mailing date. If the item was insured, also file the separate insurance claim no later than 60 days after the mailing date.

fields.label: What you get
fields.value: USPS confirms the request by email and sends periodic updates on the search. If the item is found, it is sent to the address you provide. USPS cannot always find missing mail, and some items are not forwarded for safety reasons.

fields.label: How to claim
fields.value: Check USPS Tracking first. Then submit a Missing Mail search request at missingmail.usps.com with a free USPS.com account. For Priority Mail Express, you can also request the money-back guarantee refund.

items.title: DHL Express (US): lost or damaged shipment
items.summary: DHL Express accepts cargo claims for shipments that were lost, damaged or partially delivered. Under its US domestic terms, claims must be submitted in writing within 30 days of the date DHL accepted the shipment. Without Shipment Value Protection, liability is limited to the lesser of $100 or the shipment's actual value.

fields.label: Who can file
fields.value: The party that owns the claim rights, normally the shipper. Anyone else, including the receiver, needs a written authorization (a 'release') from that party. The claim form has boxes for shipper, receiver or third party.

fields.label: Deadline
fields.value: Within 30 days from the date DHL accepted the shipment; after that DHL has no liability. One claim per shipment, and its settlement is final.

fields.label: What you get
fields.value: Up to the lesser of $100 or the shipment's actual value (the cost of replacing or reconstructing it), unless Shipment Value Protection was bought for the full value. DHL's domestic terms exclude loss caused by delay and indirect losses. With complete paperwork most claims are resolved within 30 calendar days.

fields.label: How to claim
fields.value: Complete the DHL Claim Form and email it with a copy of the waybill, invoices supporting the amount claimed (plus the online order record if bought online) and, for damage, a repair invoice and photos of the item and of the inner and outer packaging to DHL.CargoClaims@dhl.com. Keep the shipment and packaging at the delivery address; DHL may inspect it. Call 1-800-225-5345 to arrange an inspection. The decision is mailed to the claimant's address.

items.title: Target: order says delivered but did not arrive
items.summary: If a Target order shows Delivered but you cannot find it, the carrier may have marked it delivered by accident. Target says carriers typically resolve this within a day or two. If it still has not turned up, you can request a refund or a replacement from your order details.

fields.label: Who can file
fields.value: The Target account holder who placed the order, from the Target app or Target.com.

fields.label: Deadline
fields.value: Target does not state a reporting deadline on this page. Give the carrier a day or two, and check around the property, with neighbors and with your building manager first.

fields.label: What you get
fields.value: A refund or a replacement for the items you did not receive. Target emails status updates, including tracking for a replacement.

fields.label: How to claim
fields.value: Open the order under Purchases in the Target app or Orders on Target.com, select Fix an issue, choose the items you did not receive and follow the prompts. You can also call Target.com Guest Services at 1-800-591-3869.

items.title: Target: item missing from a delivered order
items.summary: If part of a Target order is missing, use Fix an issue in your order history to request a refund or a replacement. Replacements ship free as an even exchange; refunds usually go back to the original payment method.

fields.label: Who can file
fields.value: The Target account holder. Fix an issue only appears for eligible items.

fields.label: Deadline
fields.value: For Drive Up, Order Pickup or Same Day Delivery orders you can submit the request starting the day after pickup or delivery. No other deadline is stated; Target's return policy applies.

fields.label: What you get
fields.value: A free replacement, subject to availability and processed as an even exchange, or a refund to the original payment method in most cases. Amounts paid with a Target GiftCard come back as a new Target eGiftCard.

fields.label: How to claim
fields.value: Find the item under My Purchases in the Target app or on Target.com, select Fix an issue and follow the prompts. Check your order history for replacement updates. If the original item shows up later, call 1-800-591-3869.

items.title: eBay: item not received (Money Back Guarantee)
items.summary: Under the eBay Money Back Guarantee, a buyer whose item never arrived gets a refund of the full item cost plus the original shipping. Report the problem within 30 calendar days after the estimated or actual delivery date.

fields.label: Who can file
fields.value: The eBay buyer, for purchases covered by the guarantee. Not covered: items you collected yourself or shipped with your own courier, an invalid or incorrect address given at checkout, items sent on through a freight forwarder or mail redirection, deliveries you refused, in-store pickups not collected in time, and payments made partly outside eBay.

fields.label: Deadline
fields.value: Report once the estimated or actual delivery date has passed and within 30 calendar days after it. The seller then has 3 business days to respond with tracking, a delivery update or a refund. If that does not resolve it, ask eBay to step in from 3 business days up to 21 business days after you reported. You can appeal within 30 calendar days of the case closing. Event tickets: 30 days after the latest estimated delivery date or 7 days after the event, whichever is later.

fields.label: What you get
fields.value: A refund of the full item cost and the original shipping if the item was not delivered. eBay may close the case automatically if integrated tracking shows delivery to your address; orders of $750 or more also need signature confirmation to count as delivered.

fields.label: How to claim
fields.value: Go to Purchases in My eBay, select More actions next to the item, then I didn't receive it, and follow the prompts. Check your property, neighbors, building front desk and any carrier delivery photo first.

items.title: Federal rule: late or unshipped online orders
items.summary: Under the FTC's Mail, Internet, or Telephone Order Merchandise Rule, a seller must ship within the time it promised, or within 30 days if no time was stated. If it cannot, it must tell you and let you either agree to the delay or cancel for a full refund.

fields.label: Who can file
fields.value: Any US consumer who ordered goods by mail, phone, fax or on the Internet. The rule binds the seller; you use it by cancelling and asking for your money back, and by reporting a seller that does not comply to the FTC.

fields.label: Deadline
fields.value: Shipment is due within the promised time, or within 30 days after the seller receives a properly completed order (50 days if you applied for credit with the order). If the new ship date is more than 30 days late, or no definite date is given, the order is automatically cancelled unless you specifically consent to the delay.

fields.label: What you get
fields.value: A full refund of everything you paid, including shipping, handling, insurance and other costs; not just a gift card or store credit. The refund must go out within 7 working days of the cancellation (within one billing cycle when the seller is also the creditor).

fields.label: How to claim
fields.value: Tell the seller you cancel and want a refund. If you paid by credit card and the refund does not come, dispute the charge with your card issuer within 60 days of the first statement showing it. Report the seller to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

items.title: Credit card dispute for goods not delivered
items.summary: The Fair Credit Billing Act lets you dispute a credit card charge for goods you did not accept or that were not delivered as agreed. Your written dispute must reach the card issuer within 60 days after the first bill with the error was sent to you.

fields.label: Who can file
fields.value: Credit card and revolving charge account holders. Debit card rules are different and may not get you a refund for non-delivery, so contact your bank as soon as possible instead.

fields.label: Deadline
fields.value: Your letter must reach the issuer within 60 days after the first bill with the error was sent to you. After 60 days you are likely outside the Act's protection, although some issuers extend the window for delayed shipments.

fields.label: What you get
fields.value: The issuer must acknowledge your dispute in writing within 30 days and resolve it within two billing cycles, and no more than 90 days. While it investigates you may withhold the disputed amount and related finance charges; the issuer cannot collect it, close or restrict your account for disputing, or report you as delinquent for it. You must still pay the undisputed part of the bill. If the charge is correct, the issuer must explain in writing what you owe and why.

fields.label: How to claim
fields.value: Write to the issuer at its billing inquiries address (not the payment address) with your name, address, account number and a description of the error. Include copies, not originals, of receipts or order records, keep a copy of the letter, and consider certified mail with a return receipt. Contact the seller at the same time. If you disagree with the result you can appeal, and you can complain to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.
